requirement: The review prompt MUST direct the reviewer to read the `habeas` skill for directive syntax. It MUST also direct the reviewer to read the drafts as uncommitted edits to the book, the chapter around each requirement in the group, and every requirement that the group cites or overlaps.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.review_prompt.context` states only what the prompt's text must tell the reviewer to do. It must direct the reviewer to:
- read the `habeas` skill for directive syntax;
- read the drafts as uncommitted edits to the book;
- read the chapter around each requirement in the group;
- read every requirement the group cites or overlaps.

Each clause describes what the prompt says. None prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, ownership arrangement or delegation through a named interface. I tested each clause for a behavior-preserving alternative that would still violate it. There is none. Any other wording, ordering or section layout of the prompt that still gives those four directions meets the text. Any version that omits one of them fails on content alone, so the obligations are about the prompt's content. They do not constrain how it is built.

The supplied root, `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/references/review-prompt.md`, is the prompt document. Its outline is the single section `Requirement group review`, with subsections for kinds of finding, finding gaps, criteria, examples and report. It is the artifact whose content the text governs, not code with structure to map. I did not check whether its wording meets the four directions. That belongs to the behavioral and test criteria. No structural obligation needs implementation evidence, so no reference is missing.

behavioral: The requirement has four obligations for the review prompt: (1) direct the reviewer to read the `habeas` skill for directive syntax; (2) direct it to read the drafts as uncommitted edits to the book; (3) direct it to read the chapter around each requirement in the group; (4) direct it to read every requirement the group cites or overlaps.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_reads_the_syntax_drafts_chapter_and_related_requirements]` reads the real prompt through `review_prompt()`, which loads `references/review-prompt.md` from the `habeas-requirements` skill. The test collapses whitespace so wrapped lines still match. It then calls `assert_text`, which asserts `contains` for each phrase and fails with a message naming the missing one. The phrases map to the obligations as follows:
- "Read the habeas skill's `SKILL.md` first for the directive syntax" covers (1).
- "The drafts are uncommitted edits in the book: `git diff` on the book's source directory shows them" covers (2).
- "Read the surrounding chapter and every requirement the group cites or overlaps" covers (3) and (4).

The prompt is static text, so asserting these phrases is the right way to check it. It has no branches or input classes. I found no unchecked obligation or boundary case.
